personas.name: routine-lower-urinary-tract-symptoms-flexible-cystoscopy-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine referral: worsening lower urinary tract symptoms, flexible cystoscopy requested (first-line), no haematuria or bleeding-risk factors, every completeness field present — expect usually-appropriate + routine + low risk + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Worsening urinary frequency and hesitancy over 3 months — assess for bladder outflow pathology.
request.relevantHistory: No haematuria. Benign prostatic enlargement suspected.

firedRules.description: Requested flexible-cystoscopy is the recommended examination for "lower-urinary-tract-symptoms".
No red flags; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).
No bleeding-risk or active-infection factors recorded — low pre-procedure risk.

personas.name: two-week-wait-visible-haematuria-flexible-cystoscopy-antiplatelet-moderate-risk
personas.description: Painless visible haematuria aged 45 or over: flexible cystoscopy is the recommended examination for the visible-haematuria indication, and the haematuria itself independently auto-escalates triage onto the suspected-cancer two-week-wait pathway via both the red-flag rule and the NICE NG12 age/haematuria threshold, regardless of the routine urgency requested; an antiplatelet agent forces moderate bleeding risk — expect usually-appropriate + two-week-wait + moderate risk + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: One episode of painless visible haematuria last week — exclude bladder tumour.

expected.anticoagulantAction: Note antiplatelet therapy; diagnostic flexible cystoscopy is usually safe to proceed without stopping it.

firedRules.description: Requested flexible-cystoscopy is the recommended examination for "visible-haematuria".
Visible haematuria — urological assessment on the suspected-cancer pathway.
Aged >= 45 with unexplained visible haematuria — meets NICE NG12 two-week-wait criteria.
Patient is taking an antiplatelet agent — moderate bleeding risk.

flags.description: Request meets a NICE NG12 suspected-cancer two-week-wait threshold.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer on the suspected-cancer two-week-wait pathway; book the cystoscopy within 14 days.
Per BAUS, any episode of visible haematuria warrants urological assessment including cystoscopy and upper-tract imaging.

personas.name: query-referrer-catheter-problems-other-procedure-mismatch-active-uti-incomplete
personas.description: Recurrent catheter blockages with a febrile, suspected active UTI: an 'other' procedure was requested even though flexible cystoscopy is the recommended examination for the catheter-problems indication, a clear mismatch that forces appropriateness to usually-not-appropriate and the recommendation to query-referrer regardless of completeness; the active UTI independently forces high pre-procedure risk (instrumentation should be deferred until treated), and several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect usually-not-appropriate + routine + high risk + query-referrer, completeness below 100.

request.relevantHistory: Long-term catheter, recurrent blockages. Currently febrile with cloudy urine.

triage.notes: District nurse reports the catheter blocked twice this week; patient also unwell with a suspected UTI.

expected.anticoagulantAction: Defer the cystoscopy: treat the active UTI first and reschedule once the infection has resolved.

firedRules.description: Requested other is not usually appropriate for "catheter-problems"; query the referrer.
No red flags; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).
Active urinary tract infection — defer instrumentation until treated.

flags.description: Active urinary tract infection at the time of request.
flags.suggestedAction: Defer instrumentation: treat the active UTI first and reschedule once resolved to avoid urosepsis.
